intended_object: The directed system of homogeneous continuous cochain complexes C^•(G/U, X^U), with U running over the open normal subgroups of G ordered by reverse inclusion. A refinement V ≤ U gives the inflation map induced by G/V → G/U and the inclusion X^U ⊆ X^V. This is the system whose colimit computes continuous cohomology in Neukirch–Schmidt–Wingberg §2. Inferred from the docstring, the module documentation and the inflation cocone defined next to it.
explanation:
The functor sends U to `homogeneousCochains (quotientInvariants U X)`. Here `quotientInvariants U X` is X^U, the U-invariants with the subspace topology, viewed as a G/U-representation. An arrow U ⟶ V in the order dual means V ≤ U. Such an arrow is sent to Mathlib's `ContinuousCohomology.cochainsMap φ f`, which is functorial in the pair (group map, coefficient map). The group map φ is G/V → G/U (`quotientTransitionHom`, i.e. `QuotientGroup.map` of the identity of G). The coefficient map f is the equivariant inclusion X^U → X^V (`quotientTransitionIncl`). Together these give exactly the inflation transition maps C^•(G/U, X^U) → C^•(G/V, X^V).

The variance is correct: cochains are contravariant in the group and covariant in the coefficients, so the system is directed from coarse to fine. The identity and composition laws come from proved lemmas.

The setting is general: k is any topological ring and G any topological group. Indexing by open normal subgroups is the standard choice in the literature; since U is open, G/U is discrete. Mathlib has the underlying cochain functoriality (`cochainsMap`) but not this open-normal-quotient diagram, so there is no counterpart.
